rule: S_N must not be null as it serves as the primary join key
rationale: S_N is a mandatory join key with 0% missing values and serves as the one-to-one link to Acc_Info_dirty

rule: S_N must be unique across all records
rationale: S_N is described as a unique table-level identifier with 30 distinct values across 30 records

rule: Every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N
rationale: S_N is explicitly marked as a one-to-one join key with Acc_Info_dirty.S_N requiring referential integrity

rule: Account_No must be a 4-digit code
rationale: Account numbers are 4-digit identifiers ranging from 1001-1028; values should maintain consistent 4-character length

rule: Account_No should be unique unless business rules explicitly permit duplicate accounts
rationale: Evidence shows 2 duplicate values (1001, 1010) appearing twice each; flag for verification if duplicates are unintended

rule: Name must be in Title Case except for recognized lowercase particles (bin, binte, d/o, s/o)
rationale: Sample contains casing deviations: 'lim wei jie' (all lowercase) and 'WANG SHI JIE' (all uppercase); standard naming convention requires Title Case

check_params.logic: any((w[0].islower() and w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o')) or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if len(w) > 1)

rule: Gender must be consistent with gender-encoding name particles: Bin/s/o indicates Male, Binte/d/o indicates Female
rationale: Malay and Indian naming conventions use specific particles that encode gender; mismatches indicate data quality issues (e.g., 'Danish Bin Kamaruddin' should be Male)

check_params.logic: (any(p == w.lower() for w in str(row['Name']).split() for p in ['bin', 's/o']) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male') or (any(p == w.lower() for w in str(row['Name']).split() for p in ['binte', 'd/o']) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female')

rule: ID_No must follow Singapore NRIC format: one letter (S, T, F, or G), followed by 7 digits, ending with one uppercase letter
rationale: 93.3% of values follow this format; 6.6% deviate with missing prefix or 6 digits instead of 7, requiring validation

rule: ID_No must be unique across all customer records
rationale: National ID numbers should uniquely identify individuals; evidence shows duplicate 'F1011121T' requiring investigation

rule: ID_No must not be a placeholder or test value
rationale: Value 'F0000000X' appears in the dataset with a suspicious pattern (all zeros) indicating a test or sentinel value

rule: Race must be one of the standard categories: Chinese, Malay, or Indian
rationale: Dataset contains 3 semantic categories with casing variations (MALAY, malay, indian); standardization to canonical values required

rule: Gender must be either Male or Female
rationale: Column contains 4 distinct values due to casing inconsistencies (male, FEMALE); domain is binary Male/Female

rule: Age must be parseable as a numeric value
rationale: Column contains text value 'Twenty-five' which cannot be parsed as numeric despite int64 storage type

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 years inclusive
rationale: Domain constraint for human age; evidence shows negative value (-5) which is impossible

rule: Age must be at least 13 years for service account eligibility
rationale: Evidence indicates 2 values (4, -5) below 13 which may be unrealistic for a consumer service requiring customer consent

rule: Contact_No must not be null
rationale: Contact number is a mandatory business field for customer communication; evidence shows 6.7% missing values (2 NULL records)

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number (8 digits, starting with 3, 6, 8, or 9, optionally prefixed with +65 or 65)
rationale: Dataset is Singapore-based; observed formats include +65 prefix variations and local 8-digit numbers; one anomalous 7-digit value detected

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol with no whitespace
rationale: Evidence shows 4 malformed emails: missing @ ('not-an-email', 'useremail.com'), space before @ ('zx91 @example.com'), and double @ ('nabilah@@example.com')

rule: Email addresses must be unique across customers
rationale: Email is typically a unique identifier; evidence shows exact duplicate 'thm@example.com'

rule: Country must use the canonical values: Republic of Singapore, S'pore, SG, Singapore, Singapura, 新加坡
rationale: Dataset contains 8 variations of Singapore (Singapore, Singapura, S'pore, SG, SINGAPORE, singapore, Republic of Singapore, 新加坡); non-Singapore values should be flagged

rule: Street_Name must be in Title Case
rationale: One value appears in all-uppercase ('HOLLAND ROAD') inconsistent with the dominant title case pattern of Singapore street names

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() for w in str(row['Street_Name']).split() if len(w) > 1)

rule: Postal_Code must be a 6-digit code
rationale: Singapore postal codes are strictly 6 digits; evidence shows 4-digit (6907) and 5-digit (99999) values indicating missing leading zeros or data entry errors

rule: Name in Cust_Bio_dirty must match Full_Name in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N (accounting for truncation or casing differences)
rationale: S_N is a one-to-one join key; semantic consistency requires that customer names match across biographical and account tables (e.g., 'Danish Bin Kamaruddin' should correspond to 'Danish' or exact match)

check_params.semantic_check: Name should match Full_Name from Acc_Info_dirty, allowing for middle name truncation or patronymic exclusion

rule: ID_No in Cust_Bio_dirty must exactly match ID in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: S_N is a one-to-one join key; national ID must be consistent across tables (e.g., S8421753J vs S8421753X discrepancy detected in sample requires flagging)

check_params.semantic_check: ID_No must exactly match ID from Acc_Info_dirty with identical alphanumeric characters
